**Finding submitted: deviation (Section 14.1, ¶p0121), confidence 0.86.**

Summary of the analysis:

- **Assignment clause (14.1):** mutual prohibition on assignment without consent, with a mutual M&A/asset-sale carve-out — better than walk-away, but short of our preferred position.
- **Gap 1 — no affiliate carve-out:** our internal reorganizations and intra-group transfers would require Commerce One's consent.
- **Gap 2 — competitor exception cuts against us:** because the exception is symmetric, Commerce One holds a consent veto over *our* merger, acquisition or asset sale whenever the acquirer happens to compete with Commerce One. That is a de facto change-of-control consent right against us.
- **Gap 3 — no reasonableness standard** on consent anywhere in the clause.
- **Section 11 (Term and Termination):** checked for change-of-control triggers; termination arises only on uncured material breach and insolvency, so no Commerce One exit or re-pricing right on our change of control. No edit needed there.

The validated redline (ok:true) makes the minimal change: adds the affiliate/successor carve-out for Corio, confines the direct-competitor consent exception to Commerce One's own assignments (so we retain protection against Commerce One assigning to a Corio competitor), and subjects any remaining consent to "not unreasonably withheld or delayed." The comment offers the mutual notice-based fallback if Commerce One resists the asymmetry.
